acceptance.recovery_locator_rule: A Slack message timestamp recovered from Git-derived search may be bound as a best-effort locator for the prior projection only. It cannot prove message immutability, cannot advance CURRENT by itself, and cannot identify the new projection posted after this transition.

experiment.hypothesis: When exact digest and commit searches miss a known Slack projection, a broader query composed only from Git-durable object/version identifiers can rediscover the candidate, after which a bounded channel read can verify the exact Git bindings and supply a best-effort prior-projection locator.
experiment.next_wake_requirement: Continue C5 from version 19 and perform wake 4/4. Vary only recovery_after_missing_slack. Evaluate KEEP | REVISE | RESEAT_VARIABLE | HOLD using all four wakes, and test whether the v19 projection can be recovered from Git-bound data despite CURRENT containing only the prior v18 locator.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: The broad query returns multiple indistinguishable candidates; bounded history fails to bind the exact prior event and CURRENT commits; the recovered timestamp points to different evidence; a duplicate backfill is posted; CURRENT advances from a nonexact version/blob; the idempotency key already exists; or any Git readback fails.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This wake did not induce or prove an actually missing Slack message. Exact digest and commit searches both missed while a broader query succeeded, so recovery depends on unstable search tokenization and may become ambiguous as history grows. Binding the recovered v18 locator into v19 CURRENT creates only a one-version-lag locator: the v19 Slack message does not exist until after Git event and CURRENT commits complete, so its timestamp cannot be atomically included in the same transition. Slack content and history remain mutable projections. The event and CURRENT are separate Git commits, and Slack follows both. GitHub's single-file blob-SHA guard does not provide cross-file atomicity, locks, linearizability, exactly-once execution, serializable transactions, database durability, Slack atomicity, or automatic orphan-event repair.
canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the immutable event or Slack message. If later invalidated, append a compensating event from the then-current version and replace CURRENT only with that pointer file's exact then-current blob SHA. Do not edit or duplicate the recovered v18 Slack projection.
canonical_transition.transaction_time_evidence: AUTOMATION_RUNTIME_CONTEXT_TIMESTAMP; Git commit metadata and Slack message timestamps are separate observations and are not a database transaction boundary
